speaker: lead
text: Is everyone here? Right on time. Today's meeting is to prepare next quarter's team workshop. Let's aim to wrap up within twenty minutes.

speaker: member_a
text: Sounds good. I put the reference material in the shared folder yesterday. I also added the results from last year's workshop feedback survey.

speaker: lead
text: Thanks. Everyone, please read the survey results once after the meeting. We have a few things to decide today, so let's go one by one, and anything we can't settle we'll sort out separately at the end.

speaker: member_b
text: Okay, got it.

speaker: member_c
text: I'll take the minutes. I'll put each decision up on the screen as we go.

speaker: lead
text: Great. So first, let's figure out when. Has anyone pulled together some candidate dates for the workshop?

speaker: member_a
text: I checked the team calendar, and the second and third Fridays of November are relatively free.

speaker: member_b
text: The third week might be tight for me because of the month-end report. I have to hand in a draft by Thursday.

speaker: member_c
text: Either works for me. But the second Friday is the 14th, right?

speaker: member_a
text: Yes, November 14th.

speaker: lead
text: What about Thursday instead of Friday? If we do it on a Friday, I feel like everyone will just want to leave early for the weekend.

speaker: member_c
text: I actually prefer Friday. If we do it on Thursday, the next day at work will be chaos catching up on everything.

speaker: member_a
text: In last year's survey, more people said Friday worked well too. The weekend starts right after, so there's no pressure.

speaker: member_b
text: I'm for Friday as well. It feels like you just head home right after, so people will like it.

speaker: lead
text: I see. Let's go with a Friday then. Have we checked everyone else's vacation or off-site schedules? It only makes sense if all twelve of us can come.

speaker: member_a
text: Yes, nobody has requested vacation that week. There's one off-site on Wednesday, but Friday is clear.

speaker: member_c
text: Does that week clash with any other team's event? Last year it overlapped with a company-wide event and that was a pain.

speaker: member_a
text: I checked the admin team's calendar too. The company-wide event is in early December, so no overlap.

speaker: lead
text: So how about Friday, November 14th?

speaker: member_b
text: Works for me. The second week doesn't clash with the month-end report either.

speaker: member_c
text: I'm in favor too.

speaker: member_a
text: Fine by me.

speaker: lead
text: Then the date is confirmed: Friday, November 14th.

speaker: member_c
text: Friday, November 14th, noted. I'll block it on the team calendar right away.

speaker: lead
text: Next is where to hold it. Has anyone looked into possible places?

speaker: member_b
text: I checked two options. One is a training center in Gapyeong, and the other is a large meeting room at a coworking space downtown.

speaker: lead
text: What are the pros and cons of each?

speaker: member_b
text: The Gapyeong training center really gives you a change of scenery, and we can do outdoor activities. The downside is it's about an hour and a half away.

speaker: member_b
text: The downtown meeting room is easy to get to, but it's too similar to the office, so it probably won't feel like much of a break.

speaker: member_c
text: Last year when we did it near the office, everyone kept checking email and nobody could focus.

speaker: member_a
text: Right. That was the most common comment in the survey too. I think it's better to get out, even if it's a bit far. If we rent a bus, we can all travel together.

speaker: lead
text: If it's an hour and a half, what time do we need to leave in the morning?

speaker: member_b
text: If we leave from in front of the office at eight thirty, we'll get there before ten. They said traffic shouldn't be too bad on a Friday morning.

speaker: member_c
text: Eight thirty is about the same as our normal commute. That's fine.

speaker: lead
text: Is the training center available that day?

speaker: member_b
text: I called them yesterday, and November 14th is still open. They said they'll hold it if we let them know by the end of this week.

speaker: member_c
text: Does the training center have a projector or a whiteboard? I think we'll have some sit-down time in the morning.

speaker: member_b
text: Yes, the seminar room has all of that. It fits up to twenty people, so twelve is plenty of room. They have Wi-Fi too.

speaker: member_a
text: Is there a cafeteria inside the training center? Going out to eat would take quite a while.

speaker: member_b
text: Yes, there's a cafeteria inside. We just need to tell them the headcount in advance. It's a Korean buffet.

speaker: lead
text: Nice. Then let's go with the Gapyeong training center. Is everyone okay with that?

speaker: member_a
text: Yes, sounds good.

speaker: member_c
text: I'm in favor too.

speaker: member_b
text: Me too.

speaker: lead
text: Great, the place is confirmed: the Gapyeong training center.

speaker: lead
text: Next up is money. Did anyone check how much the company lets us spend per person this time?

speaker: member_a
text: Yes, I asked HR, and they cover up to 70,000 won per person. We just need to collect the receipts and submit them.

speaker: member_c
text: Does 70,000 won cover the training center rental and lunch?

speaker: member_b
text: If you divide the rental fee by headcount, it's about 25,000 won per person. Lunch at the training center cafeteria is 15,000 won.

speaker: member_c
text: And if we add the bus?

speaker: member_a
text: Renting a bus round trip would be a little over 10,000 won per person. That includes the driver's meal.

speaker: lead
text: So altogether it's about 50,000 won per person. With what's left, we could do an afternoon snack or maybe a dinner.

speaker: member_b
text: If we have a proper dinner too, we might go a bit over 70,000 won.

speaker: member_c
text: I think it's fine if everyone just has dinner on their own after we get back to Seoul. People might have plans on a Friday evening anyway.

speaker: member_a
text: Then how about using the remaining 20,000 won or so for a nicer afternoon snack? Last year there were only chips and people were a little disappointed.

speaker: member_b
text: Some fruit and coffee would be just about right.

speaker: lead
text: Okay, let's do this. We spend within 70,000 won per person, get plenty of snacks for the afternoon, and skip dinner.

speaker: member_a
text: Yes, that sounds good.

speaker: member_c
text: Agreed.

speaker: member_b
text: Fine with me too.

speaker: lead
text: Great, so the limit is 70,000 won per person.

speaker: member_c
text: 70,000 won per person, afternoon snacks, no dinner. Noted.

speaker: lead
text: Now let's decide what we'll actually do that day. How we fill the day.

speaker: member_a
text: I'd like to do a retrospective on this quarter in the morning. We never have time to do it properly.

speaker: member_c
text: A retro sounds good. But if it runs too long people get tired, so I'd cap it at about two hours.

speaker: member_a
text: Then if we split it into three parts, what went well, what could be better, and what to try next, and use sticky notes, two hours is plenty.

speaker: member_c
text: Does the training center have sticky notes and pens? If not, we should bring some from the office.

speaker: member_b
text: They said the seminar room has the basics, but it'd be good to bring a few extra packs just in case.

speaker: lead
text: During the retro, just make sure it doesn't turn into blaming people. That was a bit of a letdown last year.

speaker: member_a
text: Sure, I'll set ground rules at the start. We'll talk about the work, not the people.

speaker: member_b
text: In the afternoon I'd like to add something active. There's a walking trail near the training center.

speaker: lead
text: Is everyone okay with walking? Didn't someone mention bad knees?

speaker: member_a
text: The trail is mostly flat, so a one-hour course should be no problem. They say there's a pavilion halfway where you can rest.

speaker: member_c
text: What if it rains? The weather can be iffy in November.

speaker: member_b
text: The training center has an indoor gym, so if it rains we can switch to team games there. Like dodgeball or tug-of-war.

speaker: member_c
text: Dodgeball is a bit scary. I don't like getting hit by the ball.

speaker: member_b
text: Then let's do something like balloon volleyball. That doesn't hurt even if it hits you.

speaker: member_a
text: Nice. With balloon volleyball, we can all just laugh and play.

speaker: lead
text: Walking right after lunch might make people sleepy, so let's keep it as free time until one thirty.

speaker: member_c
text: Sounds good. We could take a quick stroll around the training center grounds during that time.

speaker: member_a
text: It'd also be nice to have a short session at the end to share next quarter's goals. So it connects with the retro.

speaker: lead
text: Good. So: retro from ten to twelve in the morning, lunch, then the trail walk from one thirty, and indoor team games if it rains.

speaker: lead
text: Then from four, thirty minutes to share next quarter's goals, and we wrap up at four thirty. Let's go with that.

speaker: member_c
text: If we leave at four thirty, we'll be back in Seoul before rush hour.

speaker: lead
text: Is everyone okay with this schedule?

speaker: member_b
text: Yes, looks good.

speaker: member_a
text: Good for me too.

speaker: member_c
text: I'm in favor.

speaker: lead
text: Then the plan for the day is confirmed.

speaker: lead
text: Finally, we need to split up who does what.

speaker: lead
text: Kenji, since you already looked into the training center and the bus, it'd be great if you handled those. And Emily, how about you run the retro?

speaker: member_a
text: I'd like to run the retro, but I have a business trip the week before, so I might not have enough time to prepare.

speaker: member_b
text: I can handle the training center, but for the bus I think I need to talk to the general affairs team first. I heard they're the ones who handle vehicle contracts.

speaker: member_c
text: I could take care of announcements and checking attendance. But I also need to look at my schedule next week before I can say for sure.

speaker: lead
text: Emily, when do you get back from your trip?

speaker: member_a
text: Wednesday night. So I'd only have Thursday.

speaker: lead
text: Hmm, everyone has their own situation, so it's hard to settle it right now.

speaker: lead
text: Let's all check our schedules this afternoon and sort it out again in the team chat.

speaker: member_a
text: Okay, I'll check my trip schedule and post in the chat.

speaker: member_b
text: I'll post as soon as I hear back from general affairs too.

speaker: lead
text: Good. So let me recap what we decided today.

speaker: lead
text: The date is Friday, November 14th, the place is the Gapyeong training center, the limit is 70,000 won per person, and the day is a morning retro and an afternoon trail walk.

speaker: lead
text: Who does what, we'll keep working out in the chat this afternoon.

speaker: member_c
text: I'll clean up the minutes and post them within an hour.

speaker: lead
text: Thanks. We finished right on time. Good work, everyone.
